about: One town, one night in 1910, one tool. Five finds, all within a few miles of each other: the trailhead, the overlook, the tool, the monuments, and the town that received the survivors. Built entirely from the research report — every find is in the ground or in Pulaski's own account.
badgeTheme: Fire service — the Big Burn, the tool, and the men of 1910

finds.groundName: Pulaski Tunnel Trailhead — Start of the Pilgrimage
finds.hint: Trailhead just south of Wallace. The big panel under the shelter.
finds.label: Read the canyon before you walk it
finds.sourceNote: Original app find list, verbatim — app site 'trail-sign' (Pulaski Tunnel Trailhead — Start of the Pilgrimage, Wallace, Idaho). Tied to this edition's catalog entry 'ID-pulaski-tunnel-trail'.
finds.task: At the Pulaski Tunnel Trailhead, find the interpretive sign and stand where the whole story is laid out — the map, the creek, the route the men ran.

finds.groundName: Pulaski Tunnel & Placer Creek Escape Route
finds.hint: You don't enter the adit; the overlook across the creek is the spot. Portal is roughly ten feet above the creek.
finds.label: Stand at the overlook, facing the adit
finds.sourceNote: Original app find list, verbatim — app site 'pulaski-tunnel' (Pulaski Tunnel & Placer Creek Escape Route, Wallace, Idaho). Tied to this edition's catalog entry 'ID-pulaski-tunnel-trail'.
finds.task: Walk Trail No. 38 to its end and stand at the overlook across the creek from the Nicholson adit portal — the hole in the ground where forty people lived through the Big Burn.

finds.groundName: Pulaski's Own Tool — Wallace District Mining Museum
finds.hint: Ask for it by his name. It's the artifact the whole town's story hangs on.
finds.label: Find the maker's own tool — the original, in the museum
finds.sourceNote: Original app find list, verbatim — app site 'wallace-tool' (Pulaski's Own Tool — Wallace District Mining Museum, Wallace, Idaho). No entry in this edition's catalog covers this ground yet; the find is carried untied.
finds.task: In the Wallace District Mining Museum, find Pulaski's own Pulaski — the Smithsonian-held tool he made — and look for his mark in the steel.

finds.groundName: Nine Mile Cemetery — the 1910 Firefighters' Monument
finds.hint: Two cobblestone monuments, raised in 1921 after Congress awarded $500. One of the five is unidentified.
finds.label: Count the names at Nine Mile
finds.sourceNote: Original app find list, verbatim — app site 'nine-mile' (Nine Mile Cemetery — the 1910 Firefighters' Monument, outside Wallace, Idaho). Tied to this edition's catalog entry 'ID-nine-mile-cemetery'.
finds.task: At Nine Mile Cemetery outside Wallace, find the two cobblestone monuments Pulaski fought twelve years to get built, and read the names of the tunnel dead.

finds.groundName: Pulaski's Own Tool — Wallace District Mining Museum
finds.hint: The trail bridge in this app's cover photo has Pulaskis mounted on its posts. Any federal engine carries three, per the current VIPR checklist.
finds.label: Hold the living descendant — a Pulaski in service today
finds.sourceNote: Original app find list, verbatim — app site 'wallace-tool' (Pulaski's Own Tool — Wallace District Mining Museum, Wallace, Idaho). No entry in this edition's catalog covers this ground yet; the find is carried untied.
finds.task: Find a Pulaski in service — on a wildland engine's rack, in a crew's hands, or mounted on the trail bridge posts — and check it against the 1911 pattern: axe one side, adze the other.

ground: Wallace, Idaho — the Pulaski Trail and the 1910 Big Burn country
name: The Pulaski Hunt

related.label: The St. Joe and the fire that filled a cemetery

about: Four finds across the Lewis-Clark Valley: a railroad bridge that still lifts for river traffic, a mill that was twice the largest white pine mill in the world (by inheritance), the valley floor it fed on — and a drive up into the white pine woods to Bovill, the junction town that existed to move logs.
badgeTheme: Timber and rail — bridges, mills, and the towns that moved the logs

finds.groundName: Clearwater River Railroad Bridge — the Lift Span at Lewiston
finds.hint: Active railroad bridge — public levee ground only, never the tracks. The lift span is the tall tower section in this app's entry photo.
finds.label: Watch the bridge that still moves
finds.sourceNote: Original app find list, verbatim — app site 'clearwater-bridge' (Clearwater River Railroad Bridge — the Lift Span at Lewiston, Lewiston, Idaho). No entry in this edition's catalog covers this ground yet; the find is carried untied.
finds.task: From the levee path on the Lewiston side, read the Clearwater River railroad bridge end to end: the 1908 truss, and the rust-brown lift towers of the span that still rises for river traffic.

finds.groundName: The Lewiston Mill — Twice the Largest White Pine Mill in the World
finds.hint: It's a working plant; the view is the visit. Steam over the stacks means the digesters are running.
finds.label: Read the mill from the river — the whole plant from one viewpoint
finds.sourceNote: Original app find list, verbatim — app site 'lewiston-mill' (The Lewiston Mill — Twice the Largest White Pine Mill in the World, Lewiston, Idaho). No entry in this edition's catalog covers this ground yet; the find is carried untied.
finds.task: Find a public viewpoint — across the Clearwater or from the Lewiston hill — and take in the whole 880-acre mill site: the plant that has worked this riverbank since the 1920s.

finds.groundName: The Lewiston Mill — Twice the Largest White Pine Mill in the World
finds.hint: The 1906 Potlatch mill held it first. Lewiston 'stole' it, in the company's own history's word.
finds.label: The title that changed hands — the 'largest white pine mill' crown
finds.sourceNote: Original app find list, verbatim — app site 'lewiston-mill' (The Lewiston Mill — Twice the Largest White Pine Mill in the World, Lewiston, Idaho). No entry in this edition's catalog covers this ground yet; the find is carried untied.
finds.task: Standing at your mill viewpoint, work the family tree: the Lewiston mill took a famous title from the older mill up the Potlatch River. Trace how the title passed, from the ground in front of you.

finds.groundName: Bovill — the Town That Moved the Logs
finds.hint: The photo in the Bovill entry is your then-vs-now: hold it up against the street in front of you.
finds.label: Stand on Bovill's main street
finds.sourceNote: Original app find list, verbatim — app site 'bovill' (Bovill — the Town That Moved the Logs, Bovill, Idaho). Tied to this edition's catalog entry 'ID-bovill'.
finds.task: Drive up into the white pine woods to Bovill and stand on the main street in this app's historic photo — the First State Bank corner, the Spokane Hotel block — in the junction town that shipped more logging crews than any town around.

ground: Lewiston, Idaho — the Lewis-Clark Valley and the Bovill woods
name: The Valley Hunt

about: Four finds up and down the valley that produced more than a billion ounces of silver: the brick town that faced the Big Burn, the canyon so narrow the trains ran through the hotel, the hotel's room count, and the 91 names at Big Creek. A drive, not a walk — Wallace to Burke is seven canyon miles, and Kellogg is down the valley on I-90.
badgeTheme: Silver — a billion ounces and the camps that dug it

finds.groundName: Wallace 1910 — the Night the Big Burn Took a Third of the Town
finds.hint: Wallace Corner and the Smokehouse are among the first brick buildings of the 1890–91 rebuild. The whole downtown is National Register-listed.
finds.label: Stand in the brick that faced the fire
finds.sourceNote: Original app find list, verbatim — app site 'wallace-1910' (Wallace 1910 — the Night the Big Burn Took a Third of the Town, Wallace, Idaho). Tied to this edition's catalog entry 'ID-wallace-brick-core'.
finds.task: Stand on Bank or Cedar Street in downtown Wallace, in the brick core that was rebuilt after the first fire and faced the Big Burn twenty years later. Look at the cornices, the brick, the 1890s faces — this streetscape is the artifact.

finds.groundName: Burke — the Town in a 300-Foot Canyon, and the Hotel the Railroad Ran Through
finds.hint: Ruins are private and unstable — the street is the viewpoint; do not enter structures.
finds.label: Measure the canyon with your eyes — creek, street, and grade in one slot
finds.sourceNote: Original app find list, verbatim — app site 'burke' (Burke — the Town in a 300-Foot Canyon, and the Hotel the Railroad Ran Through, Burke, Idaho). Tied to this edition's catalog entry 'ID-burke'.
finds.task: Drive the seven miles up Burke Canyon from Wallace and stand on Burke's single street. Look wall to wall: the creek, the street, the rail grade, and the ruins all share the same slot of ground.

finds.groundName: Burke — the Town in a 300-Foot Canyon, and the Hotel the Railroad Ran Through
finds.hint: The hotel was demolished in 1954; the street, creek, and grade running through its ground are the find.
finds.label: Stand where the trains came through the lobby — the Tiger Hotel ground
finds.sourceNote: Original app find list, verbatim — app site 'burke' (Burke — the Town in a 300-Foot Canyon, and the Hotel the Railroad Ran Through, Burke, Idaho). Tied to this edition's catalog entry 'ID-burke'.
finds.task: On Burke's main street, find the Tiger Hotel ground — where the 150-room hotel straddled the creek and the main street, and the Northern Pacific ran through its lobby under an enclosed walkway.

finds.groundName: Sunshine Mine Disaster — May 2, 1972, and the Memorial at Big Creek
finds.hint: Roadside memorial at the mouth of Big Creek Canyon. If you can, come on May 2 — Miners Memorial Day — when 91 chairs and 91 lit lamps are set out.
finds.label: Read the 91 names at Big Creek
finds.sourceNote: Original app find list, verbatim — app site 'sunshine-mine' (Sunshine Mine Disaster — May 2, 1972, and the Memorial at Big Creek, Kellogg, Idaho). Tied to this edition's catalog entry 'ID-sunshine-miners-memorial'.
finds.task: At the Sunshine Miners Memorial off I-90 near Kellogg, stand in front of Ken Lonn's 13-foot miner and read the plaque on the boulder: the names of the men lost on May 2, 1972, and Phil Batt's poem.

ground: The Silver Valley, Idaho — Wallace, Burke, and Kellogg
name: The Mining Country Hunt
tier: Road hunt — a drive, not a walk
